nodes.title: START HERE
widgets_values:
START HERE - H3 SEAMLESS CHAIN

Renders a multi-shot scene as ONE continuous take: each shot's last
frame is handed to the next shot as its first frame (the fl2va
model's trained continuation), the duplicated boundary frame is
trimmed, and the seam audio is cut at the quietest gap so words
survive the join.

RUN: write a story into the REWRITER (or paste a script - see PROMPT
SOURCE), queue once. One press renders the whole chain; the bar
sitting at 0/N at the start is the first pass over all shots, not a
hang. Output: output/video/H3CHAIN/ + a matching audio file.

RECIPE (shipped, render-verified): fl2va + beta57 + 14 steps, 243
frames/shot (~10s). Keep fps at 24 - other rates shift voice accents.
MASTER CONTROLS drives size/frames/steps AND sampler/scheduler (via
the override inputs). VRAM switches all OFF = the verified recipe.

nodes.title: ANCHORS
widgets_values:
ANCHORS (all optional; defaults = off)

IDENTITY IMAGE (gate below): seeds shot 1 from this picture (I2V).
Later shots chain as usual. Without it, identity is carried by the
frame relay + word-for-word descriptions.
CHARACTER REFS: the sampler also has a reference_images input
(unwired here) - a batch of portraits carried into EVERY shot as
<Picture 1>, <Picture 2>; bind them in the prompt text. Verified on
the ref2va checkpoint, not the shipped fl2va.
VOICE: two options, detailed on the SAMPLER note - an audio file
into voice_ref (the loader below), or self_anchor_voice which pins
shot 1's own performed voice automatically.

h3_widget_values.script:
A static camera sits at the end of the table and frames both of them from the chest up in a two-shot; the framing never changes. Live-action, shallow depth of field, fine 35mm grain. A man in his fifties with close-cropped grey hair, deep lines around the eyes and a heavy salt-and-pepper moustache, wearing a faded blue mechanic's jacket over a white t-shirt sits on one side of a late-night roadside diner booth: cracked red vinyl seats, a scratched formica table with two chipped white coffee mugs and a steel napkin dispenser, a rain-streaked window behind them reflecting an empty parking lot, and one warm pendant lamp directly above the table as the only light, the rest of the diner falling away into darkness. Across from him sits a woman in her late twenties with dark curly hair tied back, round wire-frame glasses and chipped green nail polish, wearing an oversized cream cable-knit sweater. He leans forward on his forearms, turning his mug slowly on the table, and the man in the faded blue mechanic's jacket says, "So let me get this straight. The whole street goes dark for six minutes - traffic lights, the gas station, everything - and your shop keeps its lights on." He settles back against the vinyl with both hands around his mug and waits, watching her.

nodes.title: FFLF BOUNDARY PLATES
widgets_values:
FFLF BOUNDARY PLATES  (only for continuity = flf_chain)

N shots need N+1 plates. Shot i renders BETWEEN plate i and plate
i+1, so every join is ONE shared picture instead of two independent
guesses. Four plates cover three shots.

Turn the gate ON *and* set continuity to flf_chain. With the gate
off, flf_chain stops with a clear error rather than quietly
rendering an unanchored chain.

PLATE DOCTRINE
- Generate ONE master still, then CROP the others out of it. Plates
  generated separately share a description, not a 3-D scene.
- Never carve plates out of a rendered video.
- Colour-match the set before rendering; each neighbouring pair is
  one join, so pairwise difference is what matters.
- Keep every plate at the render canvas size exactly.

Unused under context_pin - continuity rides in the latents there,
and the gate can stay off.

nodes.title: VRAM / SPEED  -  read before un-bypassing
widgets_values:
VRAM / SPEED

THE THREE PATCH NODES SHIP BYPASSED (purple), and each one needs a
pack that is NOT in this zip. A node whose class is missing kills the
whole prompt, so bypassed is the only state that queues everywhere.

  attention patch   ComfyUI-sol-attn
  chunk FFN         ComfyUI-sol-attn
                    github.com/Saganaki22/ComfyUI-sol-attn
  block cache       comfyui-minimax-h3-blockcache-T8
                    github.com/T8mars/comfyui-minimax-h3-blockcache-T8

To use one: install its pack, restart, Ctrl+B the node to un-bypass it,
THEN turn its switch on below. Both steps - un-bypassing alone changes
nothing, and flipping the switch with the node still bypassed changes
nothing either.

(SCRIPT PREVIEW in the prompt column is the same deal: it is ShowText
from github.com/pythongosssss/ComfyUI-Custom-Scripts. It is a leaf, so
leaving it bypassed costs you the on-canvas preview and nothing else.)

START HERE: every switch OFF, VRAM RESERVE at 0. That is the verified
recipe AND, on current builds, the fastest route to a working render.
The reserve measures each shape and conditioning payload as it renders
and sizes the pool itself - it has held on both 32GB and 24GB cards.
Reach for the levers below only if a render actually spills, and the
console names it when that happens rather than leaving you guessing.

Opt-in levers, in model-path order:

sol_attn - memory-efficient attention. The biggest VRAM saving at high
  resolution or long shots. Small quality risk: A/B one render before
  trusting it for a keeper.
chunk_ffn - chunks the feed-forward pass. Moderate VRAM saving, small
  slowdown, no known quality cost.
block_cache - skips near-duplicate transformer blocks. This one buys
  SPEED, not VRAM, and can soften subtle motion - keep OFF for final
  masters.
(The other toggles on the panel are not wired in this workflow and do
nothing here.)

THE THREE LEVER NODES SHIP BYPASSED (purple). They come from two
optional third-party packs, and a clean install does not have them:

  sol_attn / chunk_ffn  ->  ComfyUI-sol-attn
  block_cache           ->  comfyui-minimax-h3-blockcache-T8

Bypassed, they are dropped from the prompt entirely and the model
passes straight through, so the workflow queues without either pack.
To actually use one: install its pack, select the node, Ctrl+B to
un-bypass, THEN turn its gate switch on. Both steps are needed.

VRAM RESERVE - activation headroom on the model loader. Leave it at 0.
  A hand-set value OVERRIDES the measurement, so a number that was
  right for one shape becomes wrong for the next. Set one only to dig
  out of a spill the console has already reported.

nodes.title: LoRA stack (inert until a slot is set)
AUDIO SPINE
widgets_values:
AUDIO SPINE  (optional)

Pick a file first, THEN unmute - an unmuted loader with no file
errors the queue.

Every shot's audio locks to a slice of one continuous track. Use it
when the whole scene is a single unbroken performance: render once
at low resolution, keep the audio, then re-render at full size
against it.

Leave it muted to let the chain carry the voice itself, which is the
default path.

nodes.title: REFERENCE IMAGES
widgets_values:
REFERENCE IMAGES  (ref2va identity)

Portraits of your character, carried into EVERY shot as <Picture 1>,
<Picture 2>... Bind them in the prompt text - describe the person the
same way in every shot and the model matches them to the pictures.

Needs a ref2va checkpoint. Unlike the identity anchor above, these are
NOT a first frame: they do not constrain shot 1's composition, they
only carry who the person is.

They also cover shot 1, where the memory bank is still empty - that is
the gap they close.

Gate OFF = no references, the rest of the graph is unaffected.
One image is fine; chain more ImageBatch nodes for a third and fourth.

nodes.title: BEFORE YOU UN-BYPASS
widgets_values:
You must install the following packs first, THEN Ctrl+B the node.
Without it, un-bypassing makes the whole workflow un-queueable.

ComfyUI-sol-attn
comfyui-minimax-h3-blockcache-T8

nodes.title: WRITING
widgets_values:
WRITING FOR A CLEAN CHAIN

Two rules that cost nothing and each fix a real failure
seen in testing.

1. NAME THE SIZE AND SCREEN POSITION of any prop at the
   frame edge, in every shot's scene block.
   "a brass table lamp at the left edge, its shade level
   with his shoulder, about a third the height of frame"
   Shot 1 is the only shot with nothing pinned behind it,
   so it is the only one whose framing can disagree with
   the text. Left unstated, a lamp grew 3.8x and slid
   over ~1.7s starting exactly at the first seam, then
   held for the remaining 37 seconds. Stating it removed
   the shift across six arms.

2. NEVER NAME A NEARBY OBJECT IN A SHOT'S CLOSING BEAT.
   "She glances down at the reel" reads as a request for
   a shot of the reel - and produced exactly that, a
   close-up insert where the wide should have been.
   Keep closing beats on the speaker's own body:
   "She settles her shoulders", "He turns one hand over".

Both also protect your own measurements: texture numbers
mean nothing once the framing breaks, because they then
track content instead of drift.

nodes.title: EPISODE / BATCH
widgets_values:
EPISODE / BATCH SOURCE  (optional)

Renders a whole set of scenes by pressing Queue repeatedly.

PROMPT SET points at a file or folder of scene ideas. EPISODE INDEX
picks which one and steps by 1 on every queue, so each press renders
the next scene in the set.

Its output feeds the REWRITER's story_idea. To type an idea by hand
instead, unplug that link - your typed text is still stored on the
node underneath.

nodes.title: PROMPT SOURCE SWITCH
widgets_values:
PROMPT SOURCE SWITCH

MASTER CONTROLS -> use_file_prompts decides where the scene comes
from, and the switch is lazy so the branch you are not using never
runs:

  OFF (manual entry) - type the scene into MANUAL SCENE IDEA above.
  ON  (file / prompt set) - pull it from PROMPT SET, with EPISODE
      INDEX choosing which entry and stepping on every queue.

SHOT COUNT on the master panel drives the sampler and the prompt
writer together, so they cannot disagree. 0 means one shot per
prompt in the script, and lets the writer decide how many to
write.

nodes.title: PROMPT SOURCE
widgets_values:
PROMPT SOURCE

1. LLM: describe the scene in story_idea, queue. num_shots 0 = the model decides. base_url/model_name = any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (local servers need no key).
2. HAND-WRITTEN: mode = "passthrough (raw JSON, skip LLM)" and put {"prompts":["...","..."]} in story_idea. Plain text with shots separated by --- on its own line also works, pasted straight into the sampler's script box with the link unplugged.
3. REPEATABLE: the LLM has no seed - after a good run, copy the SCRIPT PREVIEW text into story_idea with passthrough mode.

SCRIPT PREVIEW ships BYPASSED (purple). It is the only node in this workflow from a pack that is not in the zip - ComfyUI-Custom-Scripts - so it is bypassed to keep the graph queueable without it. Install that pack and Ctrl+B the node to read the generated script on canvas; the writer feeds the sampler either way.

CLEAN-JOIN RULES (the LLM applies these via join_style; hand scripts must obey them too): open each later shot holding the previous shot's closing arrangement, ~2 quiet seconds before speech; end settled with ~2s spare; never let a line straddle two shots; repeat every character's appearance description and the room/light description word-for-word in every shot.

LOCAL WRITER? Turn on unload_model_after on the REWRITER. It frees that model from Ollama as soon as the script is written, so the video model gets the card - otherwise it stays loaded for the server's default five minutes, which is the whole of shot 1.

nodes.title: MANUAL SCENE IDEA (switch OFF)
widgets_values:
Backrooms ambient horror comedy parody, very colorful, weird entities, sarcastic ghosts, bodybuilder and cheerleader, lots of dialog, jump scares.

Fast moving found footage 90's camcorder quality recording.

nodes.title: SAMPLER
widgets_values:
SAMPLER - every dial

script: fed by SCRIPT PREVIEW; unplug to hand-edit here.
shot_count: 0 = one shot per prompt; 1-8 forces the count (extra
  prompts drop, missing ones continue the last).
size/frames/steps + sampler/scheduler: all driven by MASTER
  CONTROLS (the override inputs carry sampler/scheduler names).
seed: randomize explores; fix it to make a keeper repeatable.
seed_per_shot [ON]: measured - varying the seed per shot HOLDS the
  face; one seed for all shots drifted face AND voice. Leave ON.

VOICE
self_anchor_voice [ON]: automatic voice pin - shot 1's own audio
  becomes the reference for every later shot. Write shot 1 with a
  clean solo line. Best on a ref2va checkpoint; a wired voice_ref
  file takes priority over it.

TWO-PASS UPSCALE (needs the H3 latent-upscaler pack)
NOT usable with continuity = context_pin or latent_handoff, or
  with an audio spine - those carry raw latents / one locked
  denoise trajectory across the join and a two-pass render cannot
  preserve either. The node stops with an error naming the clash
  instead of quietly weakening the join. Available on cut,
  seamless, seamless_tail, first_frame and flf_chain.
two_pass_upscale [OFF]: every shot renders low-res through
  pass1_fraction of the steps, upscales in latent space, finishes
  at full res. Faster than native full-res, sharper than low-res.
upscale_factor [1.5]: pass-1 size = size/factor (snapped to /32).
pass1_fraction [0.4]: verified clean; past ~0.5 pass 2 cannot
  erase the upscale pattern and a ghost/moire lattice appears.
upscale_audio_denoise [0.35]: how much pass 2 may rewrite audio.
  0 locks pass-1 audio (safest for voice), 1 = full remix.

QUALITY / WORKFLOW
reference_image_size [match]: 'max' = 2048px refs, best identity,
  several times slower (ref tokens ride every step).
preview_first_shot [OFF]: writes shot 1 to output/video/
  H3_FIRSTSHOT/ the moment it decodes - cancel bad takes early.
  The full path is printed to the console.
chain_gain_control [off]: 'flatten' stops seam sharpening on long
  chains (texture ratchets ~1.3x per join; visible past ~5 shots).
  Recommended ON for chains longer than ~5 shots.

Seam audio is automatic: the boundary cut lands in the quietest
gap near each join, then a 40ms equal-power weld. A clipped word
at a join means dialogue sat too close to a boundary - see the
writing rules.

DRIFT - what is on, and what it is worth
Chained shots accrete detail: each one conditions on the
previous shot's own output, so invented texture compounds.
Measured over TEN shots at 960x544, all three of these on:

  memory_frames 0   the big one. The bank's RECENT slots
    feed accreted output forward on top of the pin. At 0
    the only reference is shot 1, which nothing has been
    added to yet. Luma 1.055 -> 1.022 per hop, chroma
    1.086 -> 1.039, and the drift stops ACCELERATING
    (4.2->6.7%/hop becomes 2.3->2.0%). Identity and
    framing held - framing actually improved.
  master_normalize luma+contrast   levels brightness AND
    contrast of the finished chain to one target taken
    from shot 1. Matching only the mean masks a contrast
    ratchet while it compounds underneath.
  pin_renorm on   holds each pinned latent at shot 1's
    sigma. The pin's own sigma climbs every hop and that
    is what the next shot is handed.

Residual is about 1.02 per hop. Not zero. Long chains
still drift, slowly.

DIALS THAT DO NOTHING HERE - verified in source, not
guessed. Under context_pin these never fire:
  join_anchor_noise  noises KEYFRAME latents; context_pin
                     creates no join keyframes
  handoff_release    belongs to continuity=latent_handoff
  bank_ref_noise     reaches bank reference IMAGES, which
                     measurement shows are not the carrier
Both are shipped at 0 so nobody tunes a dead control.

pin_noise is small and scene-dependent (-1% to -2% per
hop) and worse above 0.10. Not the fix it was called in
2.1.5.

nodes.title: REWRITER (story -> chained shot prompts)

je_widget_values.story_idea: Two people talk across a booth in a late-night roadside diner about an impossible power outage: the whole street went dark for six minutes but her repair shop kept running, its lights got brighter, and the meter outside ran backwards. He is a sceptical man in his fifties in a faded blue mechanic's jacket; she is a woman in her late twenties in an oversized cream sweater and round wire-frame glasses. One warm pendant lamp above the table is the only light, rain on the window behind them, static camera at the end of the table holding both of them in a two-shot the whole time. Four shots, one continuous conversation, no camera cuts.
